title: Conditional independence of the special-coordinate bits
statement:
Fix a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$, an achievable value $z$ of the variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$, and a pair of bits $b = (b_1, b_2)$. Write $\mu$ for the uniform measure on the sample space of the hard distribution, and let $F$ be the fiber of $Z$ above $z$, that is, the set of samples whose $Z$-value equals $z$. Denote by $X_T$ and $Y_T$ Alice's and Bob's bits at the special coordinate $T$. Then
\[
\mu(F)\cdot\mu\!\big(F \cap \{(X_T, Y_T) = (b_1, b_2)\}\big) \;=\; \mu\!\big(F \cap \{X_T = b_1\}\big)\cdot\mu\!\big(F \cap \{Y_T = b_2\}\big).
\]
hypotheses_covered: a protocol p on length-n disjointness inputs
an achievable value z of the Z variable
a pair of bits b = (b_1, b_2)
replaced: The rectangle switching identity, translated from cardinalities to the uniform hard-distribution measure.
